calls.head: The Avalanche kill penalties far better than the Maple Leafs
calls.body: On the penalty kill, Colorado is one of the league’s best, but Toronto is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Penalties should hurt the Maple Leafs more than the Avalanche.

surprises.head: A rough night for Mackenzie Blackwood
surprises.body: Blackwood allowed 5 goals on 22 shots, worth 2.2 expected goals: 2.8 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 25 starts.

surprises.head: Toronto won against the run of play
surprises.body: With chances like these, Colorado would win about 70 games in 100. Toronto won anyway.

story.head: Nylander reaches 700 points as The Maple Leafs beat the Avalanche
paras: Nick Blankenburg made his Maple Leafs debut, after playing for the Avalanche. Blankenburg got the scoring started for the Maple Leafs early in the first. Nathan MacKinnon tied it 1-1 midway through the first. The Maple Leafs’ Chris Tanev left in the first period and didn’t return. MacKinnon scored again 4:28 later to put the Avalanche ahead 2-1. William Nylander tied it on the power play midway through the second. Brock Nelson put the Avalanche ahead 3-2 later in the period. Nylander struck again 4:22 later to tie it 3-3, his 700th NHL point. Easton Cowan gave the Maple Leafs the lead 46 seconds later. Auston Matthews made it 5-3 on the power play midway through the third. Matthews scored again with 39 seconds left into the empty net with 39 seconds left. Nylander also had three assists. Matthews also had two assists.

The score flatters the Maple Leafs: the Avalanche had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Avalanche win about seven in ten. Sergei Bobrovsky was the difference, stopping 30 of 33. Mackenzie Blackwood allowed five goals on 22 shots for the Avalanche.
The Maple Leafs killed all five Avalanche power plays. The Leafs improved to 3-2-1, and the Avalanche fell to 3-2-0.

items.text: William Nylander passed Frank Mahovlich and George Armstrong for seventh on the Maple Leafs’ all-time goals list, with 297.
Nathan MacKinnon extended his point streak against Toronto to seven games.
Cale Makar extended his point streak against Toronto to six games.
One of the preview’s three calls held.
